key_insight: Training a speculative draft model to trigger rejection at critical reasoning points can improve long-horizon agent accuracy by restarting target-model verification under lower-noise conditions.
engineering_relevance: Speculative decoding may serve as a precision-allocation mechanism for coding agents, not just a speed optimization, without modifying the target model.
method: Identify critical decision points in agent reasoning traces.
Train the draft model to favor alternatives that the target model rejects at those points.
Restart verification so critical tokens receive lower-noise target-model processing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports higher end-to-end success on complex agentic coding benchmarks using frontier open-weight models while training 0.06%–0.28% of hosted parameters, but provides no numerical success gains.
watch_item: Deliberately increasing rejection could reduce decoding efficiency; the abstract does not quantify the latency trade-off.
paper_title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
